question.text:
You are evaluating three fixed income securities based on their yield and duration: Security A: Yield = 6%, Duration = 5 years Security B: Yield = 5%, Duration = 7 years Security C: Yield = 4%, Duration = 4 years
Rank the securities based on yield-to-duration ratio (Yield/Duration).

answer.text: Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: Yield-to-duration ratio = Yield / Duration. Security A: 6% / 5 = 1.20. Security B: 5% / 7 = 0.714. Security C: 4% / 4 = 1.00. Ranking from highest to lowest: A > C > B. The Trap: Option B (B, A, C) tempts those who anchor on the highest yield (6%) or longest duration (7y) without actually dividing. Option C (C, B, A) is the reversed rank. "Cannot determine" is the giving-up trap when the inputs are sufficient. Note: Source — NISM-Series-XXI-A workbook (September 2025), pages 64–68 on bond yield, price sensitivity and duration.
